correctness.rationale: On connected graph supports, tr(L+J)^{-1}-1 is strictly convex in independent edge weights because distinct edges have independent off-diagonal Laplacian entries and the Hessian is strictly positive on every nonzero feasible difference. The unique unrestricted optimizer inherits translation/reflection symmetry. Fourier diagonalization yields the exact scalar derivative and a single interior root. The verified periodized Green function G_m(c)=m/[sqrt(c(c+4))] coth[m asinh(sqrt(c)/2)] and derivative reduce the root equation to an m^2 balance. At tau=z m^{-2/3}, the stationary equation normalized by m^2 converges to 1/12-S_n/(4 z^{3/2}); strict bracketing yields the unique z_n. Substitution produces m^2/12+(z_n/4)m^{4/3}+o(m^{4/3}), with equal-budget leading term m^2/6. The standalone verifier passed 1296 checks on independently assembled Laplacians, Fourier and Green identities, and representative finite/asymptotic instances; these tests are supporting checks, not proofs of uniform asymptotics.

value.rationale: The fixed-width long-torus design is a motivated model of anisotropic physical or consensus networks with fixed total coupling resources. It exhibits a non-obvious optimal weak coupling that vanishes at an exact fractional exponent 2/3 with an explicit cross-section-dependent constant, while preserving connectivity and asymptotically halving the pseudoinverse-trace cost of equal edge resources. The theorem covers all finite rectangular tori and gives an exact two-term asymptotic; neither trivial symmetrization nor generic convexity alone supplies the singular scaling. This is a reusable structural network-allocation law rather than an isolated numerical table.
